text:
marie_product: Quick sync — proposing an audit-log archival + sampling policy for enterprise customers. TL;DR: hot 90d, cold 1y, archive up to 7y for legal holds. For cost control we sample low-risk events (e.g., debug/info) but keep 100% for auth/admin/privileged events. Looking for alignment on BYOK implications, export tooling, and launch criteria.

ajay_security: I like the buckets. Two redlines from security: 1) auth/admin events must always be immutable and 100% retained; 2) archives under BYOK must be recoverable without exposing keys to us.

lucas_eng: FWIW implementation idea: hot = ES index, cold = S3 with fast access tier (Lifecycle + Athena), archive = encrypted S3 glacier + manifest. Sampling implemented at ingestion stage with deterministic hash so we sample consistently per user/session. Example config:

```
retention:
  hot_days: 90
  cold_days: 275
  archive_days: 2190
  sample_rate: 0.05 # 5% for non-auth events
```

lucas_eng: Also proposing a hashed-index that still allows partial query by session id for sampled events — useful for investigations.

priya_legal: We need export and e-discovery hooks documented for SOC2/ISO audits. Questions: how do we surface a legal-hold flag? Who can toggle it? Is there an audit trail for toggles?

marie_product: Good Q. Proposal: legal-hold is a tenant-level flag that pins retention for specific selectors (tenant id, at-rest blobs). Toggle requires two-person approval and writes an immutable audit entry. See minimal launch criteria below.

emma_cs: From CS/customer ops: customers will ask for ad-hoc full dumps for investigations. We need a self-serve export that preserves BYOK wrapping and a signed hash for integrity. ETA expectations matter — some customers will expect <24h.

ajay_security: BYOK notes: archived objects encrypted with customer key (KMS external/bring-your-own). We must support key rotation escrow where customer can provide a rotation path or escrow token. We cannot hold plaintext. For exports, we should support a streaming unwrap where the customer provides a decryption token.

lucas_eng: Technical constraints: queryability on 1y cold tier will be expensive if we keep raw indexes. We should support two access modes: fast-search (indexes for high-value events only) and bulk-restore (batchly restore archived blobs for deep forensic queries).

marie_product: Launch criteria (MVP):
- retention tiers implemented (hot/cold/archive) and configs exposed to tenant admins
- deterministic sampling with override for events labeled "critical"
- legal-hold toggle w/ 2-approver workflow & immutable audit entries
- BYOK support for archive + documented export workflow (customer-supplied unwrap)
- SLAs: export request <72h for standard, <24h for enterprise+ticket
- QA: regression tests for retention enforcement + e2e export test using sample BYOK key

priya_legal: Also add compliance docs: mapping to SOC2 control points, and a short runbook for legal hold + export to include chain-of-custody steps.

emma_cs: For customers who need shorter retention than default (e.g., privacy-first), allow tenant overrides and a quick purge API. But must be gated by role + audit trail.

lucas_eng: Ops note: infra-bot will schedule a canary rollout of retention policies to a staging org first. infra-bot: deploy scheduled to staging-retention-canary at 2026-06-01T03:00Z.

marie_product: Next steps: 1) @lucas_eng to draft design doc with sequence diagrams + cost estimate, 2) @ajay_security to write threat model for sampling/signed archives, 3) @priya_legal to draft legal-hold compliance appendix, 4) @emma_cs to collect top-5 customer asks about export latency. Please post drafts in #product by EOD Thu. :thumbsup:

ajay_security: +1. I'll add key escrow options and whitepaper references.

lucas_eng: I'll sketch the design and include estimated $/GB for each tier and ops runbook for bulk-restore.

priya_legal: Will start draft; flag if we need vendor-friendly language for marketplace/legal.

emma_cs: I'll pull customer notes and escalate any critical SLAs.

marie_product: thanks team — keeping thread open for comments.
